title: The Pakistani Wedding Shopping Checklist (and When to Buy Each Thing)
summary: A Pakistani wedding shopping checklist ordered by time: what to buy at six months, three months, two months and two weeks before the wedding.
body_markdown:
Pakistani wedding shopping usually goes wrong for one reason: almost everything gets bought in the last three weeks. The outfits, the gifts, the decor and the home-setup items all land in the same panic window, and you end up paying the panic price for all of them.


The fix is a calendar, not a bigger budget. Work backwards from the wedding date. Anything that needs stitching, sizing, custom work or a long delivery gets ordered first. Anything cheap, fast and locally available gets left until the end, because that is where you want your flexibility.


This checklist sets out what to buy at six months, three months, two months, one month and two weeks out, then breaks the whole list down category by category. It is written for a Pakistani wedding — mehndi, baraat, walima, salami and mithai boxes included — and it assumes you will buy a fair share of it online.


## The wedding shopping timeline at a glance


If you read nothing else, read this. Each band is counted backwards from the main function.


- **6+ months out** — bridal and groom outfits, anything custom-stitched, heavy jewellery, bookings.
- **3–4 months out** — family outfits for every function, shoes, the first draft of the gift list.
- **2 months out** — bulk and imported items: decor, favours, packaging, lights, artificial flowers.
- **1 month out** — accessories, cosmetics, clutches, luggage, printing.
- **2 weeks out** — gap-filling, spares, consumables, anything you can get locally in days.
- **Final week** — buy nothing online that you cannot replace in person.


## 6+ months out: the things that cannot be rushed


The earliest band is short but it decides most of your stress level later. Two kinds of items belong here.


**Anything made to order.** The bridal outfit, the groom's sherwani, custom-embroidered dupattas, made-to-measure suits for the fathers and brothers. Hand work takes as long as it takes, and a rushed tailor is how a blouse comes back with a neckline nobody asked for. Booking the work early also gives you a real second fitting instead of a nervous one.


**Anything with a long queue.** Photographers, makeup artists, venue and catering bookings are not shopping in the strict sense, but they compete for the same weekend you do. Lock them before you buy a single gift box.


Heavy or statement jewellery belongs here too if it is being made. If you are buying ready pieces rather than commissioning them, you have more room — but decide the metal tone early, because every dupatta, clutch and sandal you buy afterwards has to sit next to it.


## 3 to 4 months out: family outfits and the first real list


This is when the list stops being an idea and becomes a spreadsheet. A Pakistani wedding is not one event, so plan per function: mehndi, baraat, walima, plus the smaller dholki and mayoun evenings.


- **Outfits for the immediate family, per function.** Count heads, count events, and write both down. Most overspending happens because somebody's mayoun outfit is remembered two weeks before.
- **Shoes.** Order early for one boring reason: you need time to exchange them. Wedding shoes get worn standing for six hours. A size that is almost right in the box is not right at 1am on a stage.
- **The gift list, in draft.** Who gets what, roughly. You do not have to buy yet, but you need the head count now, because the gift list drives the biggest bulk order you will place.


If you are buying outfits online, this band is also the moment to test a seller with one small order before you commit the family's wardrobe to them. Our guide on[where to buy ladies fashion online in Pakistan](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/where-to-buy-ladies-fashion-online-in-pakistan) covers what to check before you scale up an order.


## 2 months out: the window for bulk and imported items


Two months is the single most useful marker on this whole checklist, and it exists because of delivery time.


Anything ordered direct from China through Markaz lands in roughly 10–17 days. That is fast enough to be practical and slow enough that you must plan for it. At two months out you have room for the order to arrive, for you to open the cartons, check quantities, and reorder anything short — and still be finished with a month to spare.


What belongs in this band:


- **Decor and stage items** — artificial flowers, fairy lights, drapes, lanterns, table runners, backdrop props.
- **Favours and giveaways** — small gifts for guests, bought in one quantity rather than in five panicked trips.
- **Packaging** — gift boxes, ribbons, organza pouches, salami envelopes, mithai box sleeves.
- **Mehndi night supplies** — decorated thaals, bangles in bulk, hair accessories, props for the entry.
- **Anything you need in a matching set of thirty** — because a matching set is exactly what local markets run out of first.


This is the part of a wedding budget where buying direct actually changes the number, since decor and favours are almost entirely imported goods with a local margin stacked on top. You can browse the imported catalogue by category on[Markaz China categories](https://www.markaz.app/china/categories) , and there is no minimum order, so a set of thirty is a real order rather than something you have to negotiate up to a carton.


One caution: order a few spares of anything you are buying in bulk. Breakage happens, and matching a replacement later is harder than buying five extra now.


## 1 month out: accessories, beauty and the detail list


By now the big shapes are decided, and the remaining work is everything that finishes them.


- **Jewellery and accessories per outfit** — earrings, bangles, maang tikka, hair pins. Lay each set next to the outfit it belongs to rather than buying in the abstract.
- **Clutches and bags** for each function.
- **Cosmetics and skincare.** Buy skincare earlier than makeup — anything going on the bride's face should have been used for weeks, not opened the night before. Our guide to[buying beauty and cosmetics online in Pakistan](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/where-to-buy-beauty-cosmetics-online-in-pakistan) covers how to check a seller before you order.
- **Luggage** if there is travel after the wedding.
- **Printing** — invitation cards if not already done, plus place cards, tags and signage.


Costume and imitation pieces do most of the work at a Pakistani wedding, because you need different tones for different functions and you are not going to commission four sets. If you are comparing options,[artificial jewellery brands in Pakistan](https://www.markaz.app/blog-post/best-artificial-jewellery-brands-in-pakistan) is a useful starting point.


## 2 weeks out: local, fast, cash on delivery


The last useful online window. Delivery within Pakistan on Markaz runs about 3–5 days, so two weeks gives you one comfortable order and, if something is wrong, time for one replacement.


Keep this band for gaps rather than plans: the extra dupatta pins, the second set of bangles, spare gift boxes, the phone stand for the photographer, batteries for the fairy lights. Pay cash on delivery where you can. It keeps the money tied to parcels that actually arrive, which is a genuinely useful budget control in a month when five people are spending on the same event.


## The final week: stop ordering


In the last seven days, buy only what you can walk into a shop and replace the same day. This is not about trust; it is about time. Any order placed now has no room for an exchange, a wrong size or a delayed courier, and chasing a parcel is the last thing you need in that week. Write down whatever is still missing, hand the list to whoever is free, and let them buy it locally.


## The category-by-category checklist


Use this as the master list, then drop each line into the time band above.


### Outfits


Bridal outfit · groom's sherwani or suit · mehndi outfits · walima outfits · outfits for parents and siblings per function · dupattas and shawls · stitching and fittings booked.


### Jewellery and accessories


Main bridal set · lighter sets for mehndi and walima · bangles and chooriyan · maang tikka, jhumar, nath · hair accessories · watches and cufflinks · clutches per outfit.


### Shoes and bags


Khussas or heels per function · a comfortable backup pair the bride can actually stand in · men's formal shoes · travel bag.


### Beauty


Skincare started well in advance · makeup, if not provided by the artist · hair tools · nail supplies · perfume.


### Gifts and guest items


Salami envelopes · mithai boxes and sleeves · favours for guests · gifts for the other family · gift wrapping and tags.


### Decor and functions


Mehndi thaals and props · artificial flowers · fairy lights and lanterns · stage backdrop items · table runners and centrepieces · cushions and floor seating for the dholki.


### Home setup


Bedding and bed sets · kitchen basics · storage · small appliances · towels and linen. This is the longest list of all, and the one most worth ordering early and in one go rather than in weekly trips.


### Paper and logistics


Invitation cards · guest list and seating notes · signage · thank-you cards · a printed master checklist somebody other than the bride is holding.


## How to keep the budget from drifting


Wedding budgets rarely break in one large purchase. They break in forty small ones that nobody wrote down.


- **One sheet, one owner.** A single shared list with a column per function. Two people buying gifts separately is how you end up with duplicates.
- **Buy by function, not by shop.** Tick off a whole event at a time so you can see what is genuinely missing.
- **Use cash on delivery as a control.** Paying on arrival keeps spending tied to deliveries landing, and it is far easier to reconcile at the end of the month.
- **Keep orders in fewer places.** Ten sellers means ten tracking numbers, ten return policies and ten arguments. Fewer, larger orders are easier to chase.
- **Set a spares line.** Assume a small share of bulk items will break or be short, and budget for it instead of being surprised by it.


## Where to buy each part of the list


Most families end up using three channels, and the trick is matching the channel to the item rather than loyalty to one of them.


**Physical markets** — Liberty and Anarkali in Lahore, Tariq Road and Saddar in Karachi, Raja Bazaar in Rawalpindi. Best for anything you need to touch: fabric, heavy outfits, the bridal dupatta, shoes you want to try. You pay for the convenience, and you spend a day per trip.


**Local online sellers** — good for restocks and for anything needed inside two weeks, with cash on delivery keeping the risk low. Buying direct removes the importer's margin, which is where the saving on a large order comes from. ## Mistakes that cost Pakistani families money


- **Leaving decor to the end.** It is the most import-heavy part of the list and the one that most rewards ordering early. Left to the last fortnight, it becomes the most expensive part instead.
- **Ordering shoes with no exchange window.** Sizes vary between sellers. Order with weeks to spare, not days.
- **Matching shades on a screen.** Dupatta and jewellery tones rarely read true in a photo. Buy the outfit first, then match accessories to the actual piece in your hand.
- **Buying bulk items exactly to count.** Order spares. Matching a replacement later is the hard part.
- **Prepaying an unknown seller.** On a wedding budget this is the one risk worth removing entirely. Prefer cash on delivery on an established marketplace.
- **No single list.** The duplicates and the forgotten mayoun outfit both come from the same missing spreadsheet.


## Frequently asked questions


**How early should wedding shopping start in Pakistan?** Six months before the main function for anything custom-stitched or made to order. Three to four months for family outfits and shoes. Two months for bulk and imported items. Everything else fits comfortably in the last month.


**What is actually worth ordering from China?** Decor, favours, gift packaging, lights, artificial flowers, bangles and hair accessories — anything you need in quantity and in a matching set. Order it about two months out so there is room to check the shipment and reorder if something is short.


**Is it safe to buy wedding items online?** Yes, with two habits: buy on an established marketplace rather than an unknown page, and use cash on delivery so no money leaves your hands until the parcel is at your door. Leave enough time that a replacement is still possible.


**What should I never buy online for a wedding?** The bridal outfit, if it needs fitting, and anything bought in the final week. Fabric and heavy embroidery are worth seeing in person. Everything else — decor, gifts, accessories, home items — is straightforward online if you order in time.


**How do I stop the budget drifting?** One shared list with a column per function, one person owning it, cash on delivery so spending matches deliveries, and a small spares allowance built in from the start.
